standard.title: Estimation strategies
standard.description: Check and explain the reasonableness of solutions to problems including financial contexts using estimation strategies appropriate to the context
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use equal sharing and grouping strategies (AC9M1N06). They have not yet applied formal estimation strategies to check reasonableness in financial or multi-step contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students check and explain the reasonableness of solutions using appropriate estimation strategies including in financial contexts.

nodes.label: Estimation strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply rounding and front-end estimation to approximate a calculation result before or after computing.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply rounding to estimate the result of a calculation; compare the estimate to the computed answer.
nodes.typical_width: Apply and compare front-end, rounding and compensation strategies; choose the most appropriate strategy for a given calculation; explain why an estimate is sufficient or insufficient.
wider: Use estimation to budget within financial scenarios
Investigate how estimation is used in scientific measurement and reporting

response_modes.reason: Different estimation strategies suit different number types. Students need exposure to multiple strategies to select appropriately rather than defaulting to rounding in all cases.

nodes.hinge_reason: Estimation strategy repertoire is required by Node 2 — students who can only round cannot evaluate reasonableness across varied calculation types, including those where rounding produces misleading estimates.
success_criteria: Student produces a reasonable estimate using a named strategy
Student explains the strategy used and why it is appropriate

nodes.label: Reasonableness judgement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate whether a given answer to a problem is reasonable using estimation, and explain their judgement.
nodes.minimum_width: Given a problem and a proposed answer, use estimation to judge whether the answer is reasonable; explain the reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Apply reasonableness checks to multi-step problems and financial contexts; identify common error types (e.g. operation error, magnitude error) by inspecting the relationship between estimate and answer.
wider: Analyse real-world calculation errors (e.g. news reports, budgeting mistakes) and use estimation to identify the error
Design 'unreasonable answer' problems for peers to identify

response_modes.reason: Reasonableness judgement is highly context-dependent. Students need varied contexts to develop genuine evaluation skill rather than mechanical rounding followed by a yes/no answer.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real error analysis and problem design give advancing students purposeful, authentic tasks.
success_criteria: Student correctly judges whether a given answer is reasonable
Student explains their judgement using an estimation strategy

nodes.label: Estimation in financial contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply estimation strategies to check the reasonableness of solutions in financial contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply an estimation strategy to a financial problem (e.g. estimating total cost); judge whether the exact answer is reasonable.
nodes.typical_width: Apply estimation across a range of financial contexts (shopping, budgets, change); identify when estimation is sufficient vs when exact calculation is needed; communicate reasoning.
wider: Analyse a household budget scenario using estimation to identify whether it is viable
Investigate how financial journalists use estimation to convey magnitudes

response_modes.reason: Financial contexts have diverse estimation demands: shopping (round up), budgeting (round conservatively), reporting (order of magnitude). Multiple contexts build contextual judgement about appropriate precision.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Real financial analysis contexts are rich and purposeful for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student applies an estimation strategy correctly in a financial context
Student judges whether the exact answer confirms or contradicts the estimate
